Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 46, verse 4–6:

{4} That is: {Say}: to these who associate with Allah idols and rivals that possess no benefit, no harm, no death, no life, and no resurrection. Say to them, making clear the impotence of their idols and that they do not deserve any of worship: {Show me what they have created from the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens?} Have they created any of the bodies of the heavens and the earth? Have they created mountains? Have they made rivers flow? Have they produced animals? Have they caused trees to grow? Did they have any assistance in creating any of that? None of that, by their own admission about themselves, let alone about others. This is a decisive rational proof that everything other than Allah, worshipping it, is void.
Then he mentioned the absence of a transmitted proof, saying: {Bring me a Book before this}: a Book that calls to association, {or a remnant of knowledge}: a transmitted tradition from the messengers that commands this. It is known that they are unable to bring from any of the messengers a proof that indicates this. Rather, we affirm with certainty that all the messengers called to the monotheism of their Lord and forbade association with Him, and this is the greatest knowledge transmitted from them. Allah the Exalted said: {And We certainly sent into every nation a messenger, [saying], "Worship Allah and avoid the taghut"}, and every messenger said to his people: {Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him}. Thus it is known that the disputation of the polytheists regarding their association is not based on any proof or evidence, but they relied on false assumptions, corrupt opinions, and defective minds. The examination of their circumstances, the tracing of their sciences and their deeds, and the consideration of the state of those who spent their lives worshipping it, will show you their corruption: did it benefit them anything in this world or in the Hereafter?

{5–6} For this reason Allah the Exalted said: {And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, while they are unaware of their supplication}; that is, for the duration of their stay in the world, they benefit him not an atom's weight. {And they, of their supplication, are unaware}: they do not hear their supplication, nor do they answer their call. This is their state in the world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will disavow your association, and when people are gathered they will be enemies to them, cursing one another and disassociating from one another, and they were, in their worship of them, disbelievers.

{15} This is from His kindness to His servants and His gratitude toward parents: He enjoined children and charged them to be good to their parents with gentle speech, soft words, spending wealth and provision, and other forms of kindness. From this verse, together with His saying ﴿And the mothers suckle their children for two full years﴾, it is inferred that the minimum period of pregnancy is six months, because the period of nursing, which is two years, when subtracted from thirty months, leaves six months as the period of pregnancy. ﴿Until he reaches his maturity﴾, that is, the limit of his strength, his youth, and the completion of his intellect; ﴿and reaches forty years, he says, "My Lord, inspire me"﴾, that is, grant me the inspiration and success, ﴿to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents﴾, that is, the favors of religion and the favors of this world. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 46, verses 21–26:

So he commanded them to worship Allah, which encompasses every sound saying and praiseworthy deed, and forbade them from association and rivalry (with Allah), and warned them of severe punishment if they did not obey him. But that call did not benefit them.

{22} {They said: "Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods?"}; that is: you have neither a purpose nor any truth with you except that you have opposed our gods, so you wish to turn us away from them. {Bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful}. This is the utmost of ignorance and obstinacy.

{23} {He said: "The knowledge is only with Allah"}: He is the one in whose hand are the reins of affairs and their keys, and He is the one who will bring you the punishment if He wills. {And I convey to you what I have been sent with}; that is, there is upon me only the clear conveyance. {But I see you to be a people who are ignorant}: and therefore there proceeded from you what proceeded of this severe audacity.

{24–25} Then Allah sent upon them the great punishment, which was the wind that destroyed them and annihilated them. Hence He said: {Then when they saw it}; that is, the punishment, {as a cloud approaching their valleys}; that is, spreading across like a cloud, approaching their valleys which flow and water their crops and from whose wells and pools they drink. {They said}, rejoicing: {This is a cloud that will bring us rain}; that is, this cloud will rain upon us. Allah, exalted is He, said: {Rather, it is that which you were impatient for}; that is, this is what you brought upon yourselves when you said: {Bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful}. {A wind wherein is a painful punishment, destroying everything}: it passes over everything with its severity and ill omen. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 46, verse 34–35:

{34} He (Exalted is He) informs us of the dreadful state of the disbelievers when they are presented before the Fire, which they used to deny. They will be rebuked and it will be said to them: ﴿Is this not the truth?﴾; for you have been brought near to it and have witnessed it with your own eyes. ﴿They will say: "Yes, by our Lord!"﴾ So they acknowledge their sins, and their lies are made plain. ﴿He will say: "Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve."﴾ That is: a punishment that is constant and everlasting, just as your disbelief was an enduring attribute.

{35} Then He (Exalted is He) commanded His Messenger to be patient with the harm of the deniers who opposed him, and to never cease calling them to Allah, and to follow the patience of the ulul-'azm (the possessors of resolve) among the Messengers, the masters of creation, the people of firm resolve and lofty aspirations, whose patience was great and whose certainty was complete. They are the most worthy of creation to be emulated, to have their traces followed, and to be guided by their beacon. So he (ﷺ) complied with the command of his Lord and was patient with a patience that no prophet before him had shown, until those who opposed him shot at him from one bow, and they all united to bar him from calling to Allah, and did whatever they could of enmity and warfare. Yet he (ﷺ) never ceased proclaiming the command of Allah, remaining steadfast in striving against the enemies of Allah, patient over the harm he received, until Allah established him in the land, made His religion prevail over all other religions, and made his community prevail over the nations. May the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him abundantly.

And His saying: ﴿So do not seek to hasten [the punishment] for them﴾; that is, for these deniers who seek to hasten the punishment. This is from their ignorance and foolishness; so let not their ignorance make you feel weak, nor let their haste lead you to invoke Allah against them for that. For everything that is coming is near. And ﴿as if they, on the day they see what they are promised, had not remained [in the world] except an hour of a day﴾; so do not grieve over their brief enjoyment while they are heading toward a severe punishment. ﴿A message﴾; that is, this worldly life, its enjoyments, desires and pleasures, is a troubled provision and a passing of a short, present time. Or, this great Qur'an, in which We have clarified for you a complete clarification, is a message for you and a provision for the Hereafter. How excellent a provision and sustenance it is: a provision that reaches the Abode of Bliss and protects from the painful punishment. It is the best provision that creatures can take with them, and the greatest blessing with which Allah has favored them. ﴿Will any be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾ That is: those in whom there is no good, who have departed from the obedience of their Lord, and who did not accept the truth that the Messengers brought them. Allah has given them an excuse and warned them. So, after that, when they persist in their denial and disbelief, we ask Allah for protection.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Ahqaf. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.

How excellent a provision and sustenance it is: a provision that reaches the Abode of Bliss and protects from the painful punishment. It is the best provision that creatures can take with them, and the greatest blessing with which Allah has favored them. ﴿Will any be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?﴾ That is: those in whom there is no good, who have departed from the obedience of their Lord, and who did not accept the truth that the Messengers brought them. Allah has given them an excuse and warned them. So, after that, when they persist in their denial and disbelief, we ask Allah for protection.

End of the commentary on Surah al-Ahqaf. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
